a plain push after a one-post pull: 0 of 331 unread documents sent (330 seeded posts + 1 comment under another post)

body:
CL17 was not stupid: the kit handed it a push of 330 writes it had never read and then refused every way out. Now a part sends only its own post and its comments, a pull is always allowed (it rebuilds whatever was waiting), and the two generated cards no longer leave conflict comments.

### What went wrong for CL17
A one-post pull loaded only the part's post and the cards. The local board then held about 330 other documents the copy had never read from the Artifact (a git seed, or writes the board server made after the load). These had no base and no version, so `artifact push` diffed the whole local copy and built them all as unpinned writes. The push had no single-post option. The guard refused a hand-made write. It also refused a pull while those batches waited, and the batches could not go out without a pull. That is a deadlock: the part tried four ways and stopped.

### What changed
1. **`kit.py artifact push --post <id>`** builds only that post and the comments whose `post_id` is it. Activity rides are left out. The post is pinned to the version recorded at load: the scoped pull now tells the part to run `artifact load posts/<id>=<N>` with the N the get reply names.
2. **A read scope.** A `--post` pull marks the copy as partial and records what it read: the posts fetched by id, and the comments under the part's post. Every load adds the documents it loaded. In a partial copy, a push skips anything outside that scope and names how many it skipped. Those documents also no longer count as "not sent", so the Stop hook stops nagging about them. A `pull --full` makes the copy whole again.
3. **A pull never deadlocks.** If batches are waiting, `artifact pull` drops them and removes the record the guard reads (pending.json), so the pull's own calls go through. The next `artifact load` rebuilds those batches the same way (`--post` kept) against what the pull brought, and prints them. The documents of the dropped batches are not mistaken for a git seed by that load. If a batch had in fact reached the Artifact, it comes back with the pull as the live copy, so nothing is written over it.
4. **Generated cards.** In `artifact reconcile`, when _dashboard or _trains changed on both sides, the newer build wins with no conflict comment. Posts and comments keep CL45's both-sides rule.

### Tests (tests/test_cl59_part_push.py)
The tests use a real local board server and the kit's own functions, with a git remote for the reconcile case.
- `test_push_post_builds_only_its_post_and_comments_pinned`: CL17's copy (a one-post pull, 330 unread posts on the board, the post edited, 2 comments plus 1 under another post) gives exactly 3 writes, with the post at if_version 4.
- `test_cli_push_post`: the same through the command line.
- `test_a_push_after_a_partial_pull_never_sends_what_it_did_not_read`: a plain push skips the 331 unread documents, and none of them count as unsent.
- `test_a_full_pull_reads_the_whole_board_again`
- `test_a_pull_while_batches_wait_rebuilds_them`
- `test_load_refuses_a_bad_version`
- `CardsNeverConflict.test_generated_cards_take_the_newer_build`
differs: CL59: builds on CL16 (the board travels in git) and CL45 (web reconcile); neither lets a part push only its own post nor stops a pull deadlocking on waiting batches. CL59 adds both.
handoff:
- A part's turn 1: after `artifact pull --post <id>`, run `artifact load posts/<id>=<N>` with the version the get reply names; then `artifact push --post <id>` builds only that post's writes, already pinned.
- The orchestrator's sync no longer writes conflict comments on _dashboard or _trains; any already on the board can be deleted by hand.
- An earlier load used to mark a document this copy created but had not sent yet as a git seed and never send it. That is now fixed for the documents of dropped batches and for creates under a part's own post; on a whole-board copy, a create made before a load is still treated that way.

- `done` refused every step: the code behind decision D1 (the AI link's drop box, commit 75a4f41) was only on feat/streamline-doctor-memory, never on main. In full-auto mode its default applied: CL59 cherry-picked 75a4f41, so it reaches main with this step. That branch's other commits are untouched.
not_checked: not tried against the live Artifact with a real ArtifactData batch from a second part session; the replay uses a real local board server and the kit's own functions
the guard hook itself is unchanged: the pull frees it by removing the waiting-batch record it reads

A part sends its own post to the live board in one command, never other sessions' writes.

Owner, 2026-11-27 (screenshot of CL17's session): "How did it have so many failed commands? Was it stupid?" CL17 pulled only its own post (`artifact pull --post`), then `artifact push` diffed the whole local copy against that partial pull and built 330 unpinned writes; the push has no single-post option, the guard refuses a hand-made ArtifactData write, and refuses a pull while built batches wait. The part tried four ways and stopped. Web orchestrator 2 hit the same today: hand-filtering batches, conflict comments on _trains at every sync.

1. `kit.py artifact push --post <id>` (and the comments it wrote) builds only those writes, pinned to the versions read.
2. A push after a partial pull never sends documents the pull did not read.
3. A pull is allowed while batches wait: it rebuilds them after loading, never deadlocks.
4. The generated cards (_dashboard, _trains) are never a two-sided conflict: the newer build wins, no conflict comment.
5. Tests for each; replay CL17's case and count writes (1 post + its comments).
title: A part pushes only its own post; a pull never deadlocks on waiting batches
verdict: A part's push now carries only its own post and comments, pinned to the versions it read; a push never sends what its pull did not read; a pull no longer deadlocks on waiting batches.
